title: Grade 11 Chemistry National Exam & Practice 2015 (6 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 6 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following illustrates an extensive property?
options: Doubling the volume of a sample also doubles the mass; so the ratio of mass to volume remains the same.
If water in two beakers at the same temperature are mixed to make a single quantity of water and the temperature of the combined quantity of water is the same as it was in the two separate beakers.
The electrode potential at standard condition for the half-reaction Cu²+ + 2e- --> Cu is the same as for 2Cu²+ + 4e- --> 2Cu.
If a system is divided into parts and it is found that the property of the complete system has a value that is the sum of the values of the property of all the parts.
questions.explanation: An extensive property is a physical quantity whose value is proportional to the amount of substance (e.g., mass, volume, total energy).

questions.questionText: The number of digits to the right of the decimal point denotes:
questions.explanation:
Decimal places refer to the number of digits written to the right of the decimal point in a number.

 Significant figures indicate the total number of meaningful digits in a number, scientific notation expresses numbers in the form of a × 10ⁿ, and conversion factor is used to convert units.

questions.questionText: A student uses a digital balance ( 0.02), a thermometer (0.1), a measuring cylinder (0.05), and a beaker (0.5) during an experiment. Which of the above instrument is more precise?
questions.explanation:
Precision is indicated by the smallest increment of measurement or the instrument's uncertainty.

 The instrument with the smallest uncertainty is the most precise.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following IS TRUE about isotopes?
options: Isotopes of the same elements contain the same number of neutrons.
Isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties.
Isotopes of an element are atoms that have different number of electrons and protons.
Isotopes of an element are identical in mass number.
questions.explanation:
Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

 Since chemical properties depend on the number of protons (and thus electrons), isotopes of an element exhibit the same chemical behavior even though their masses differ.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following describes the quantum mechanical model?
options: An atom is a sphere with a positively charged matter, in which electrons are embedded.
Electrons moved around the nucleus of an atom in circular orbits.
The locations of electrons in an atom are described in terms of probability.
An atom is represented by a solid indestructible sphere.
questions.explanation:
The quantum mechanical model of the atom describes electrons as existing in regions of space called orbitals, where the probability of finding an electron is highest.

 Earlier models, such as the Thomson model, Rutherford model, and Bohr model, do not accurately describe the probabilistic nature of electron positions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the diagrammatic representation of $^{35}	ext{Cl}$?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains that light has BOTH wave and particle nature?
options: Microscopic systems, such as atoms and molecules can possess wave properties.
Light consists of electromagnetic waves which have an oscillating electric and magnetic disturbance that spreads electromagnetic radiation.
beam of light is a stream of particles of electromagnetic energy, with energy proportional to the observed frequency of the light.
An electron that is bound to the nucleus behaves like a standing wave and its position is given in terms of probability.
questions.explanation:
The dual nature of light is described by wave-particle duality. 

Light behaves as an electromagnetic wave (oscillating electric and magnetic fields) and also as a stream of particles called photons, each carrying energy E = hν proportional to its frequency.

 The other options describe wave behavior of matter or purely wave characteristics of light.

questions.questionText: A nuclear breakdown in which particles or electromagnetic radiation is emitted is:
questions.explanation:
Radioactive decay is the process by which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by emitting particles (alpha, beta) or electromagnetic radiation (gamma rays).

 Radioactivity refers to the general phenomenon, radioactive isotopes are the unstable nuclei themselves, and radio waves are a type of electromagnetic radiation unrelated to nuclear breakdown.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main reason for the large difference in dipole-moment between the triatomic molecules water (H₂O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂)?
options: The presence of multiple bonds in carbon dioxide (CO₂) while single bonds in water .
The bonds in carbon dioxide (CO₂) are directed 180° and bond polarity reinforces each other.
The presence of lone pairs of electrons in water (H₂O) partially reinforces bond polarities.
The higher electronegativity difference among atoms in water (H₂O) than in carbon dioxide (CO₂).
questions.explanation:
Water (H₂O) has a bent molecular shape due to the presence of two lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom.

 This bent geometry causes the individual O–H bond dipoles to partially reinforce each other, resulting in a significant net dipole moment.

 In contrast, carbon dioxide (CO₂) is linear with bond angles of 180°, so the C=O bond dipoles cancel each other, giving CO₂ a zero net dipole moment.

questions.questionText: How many non-bonding pairs of electrons are present in the valence shell of the central atom in ClF₃?
questions.explanation:
In ClF₃, chlorine is the central atom with 7 valence electrons. 

Three electrons are used to form three Cl–F bonds, leaving four electrons unshared.

 These four electrons form two non-bonding (lone) pairs. According to VSEPR theory, this results in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

questions.questionText: Which one would be observed in a laboratory activity that is applied on naphthalene?
options: It shows relatively high melting point.
It conducts electricity in molten state.
questions.explanation:
Naphthalene is a non-polar covalent organic compound. 

According to the principle 'like dissolves like', non-polar substances dissolve in non-polar solvents such as benzene.

 Naphthalene is insoluble in water, has a relatively low melting point compared to ionic solids, and does not conduct electricity in either solid or molten state.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: In Lewis model, electrons repel one another and a pair of bonding electrons lies far apart as possible.
Valence-bond model explain molecular shape from the interaction of atomic orbitals.
Valence bond model simply shows the linkage between atoms and the presence of lone pairs.
Lewis model predicts the shapes of molecules based on electron-pair repulsions around a central atom.
questions.explanation:
The valence-bond model explains molecular shape by considering the overlap and interaction of atomic orbitals, often through hybridization.

 The Lewis model mainly shows electron distribution and bonding but does not accurately predict molecular shapes based on electron-pair repulsions—that role belongs to VSEPR theory.

questions.questionText: The energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous ions is called:
questions.explanation:
Lattice energy is the energy required to completely separate one mole of an ionic solid into its constituent gaseous ions.

 It is a measure of the strength of the electrostatic forces holding the ions together in the crystal lattice.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an ionic compound?
questions.explanation:
CaCl₂ (calcium chloride) is an ionic compound formed from a metal (calcium) and a non-metal (chlorine).

 The other options are covalent compounds: PCl₃ (phosphorus trichloride), H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide), and CO₂ (carbon dioxide) consist of non-metal atoms sharing electrons.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following results from interaction of the atomic orbitals of bonding atoms to produce new electron distribution associated with the entire molecule?
questions.explanation:
Molecular orbitals are formed when atomic orbitals from bonding atoms combine, producing new orbitals that extend over the entire molecule.

 These orbitals describe the probability distribution of electrons in the molecule.

 Hybrid orbitals result from mixing atomic orbitals on the same atom, not over the entire molecule

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of molecular crystals?
questions.explanation:
Molecular crystals are composed of molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces such as Van der Waals forces or hydrogen bonds.

 Solid CO₂ (dry ice) is an example, where CO₂ molecules form a crystalline lattice. 

Magnesium is a metallic crystal, diamond is a covalent network crystal, and NaCl is an ionic crystal.

questions.questionText: What are the four quantum numbers for an electron in a 2s orbital?
questions.explanation:
The four quantum numbers are:

- Principal quantum number (n) = 2 (for the second shell)

- Azimuthal quantum number (l) = 0 (for s-orbital)

- Magnetic quantum number (mₗ) = 0 (since l = 0)

- Spin quantum number (mₛ) = +1/2 (one of the two possible spin states).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: In Lewis model, electrons repel one another and a pair of bonding electrons lies far apart as possible.
Valence-bond model explain molecular shape from the interaction of atomic orbitals.
Valence bond model simply shows the linkage between atoms and the presence of lone pairs.
Lewis model predicts the shapes of molecules based on electron-pair repulsions around a central atom.
questions.explanation:
The valence-bond model explains molecular shape by considering the overlap and interaction of atomic orbitals, often through hybridization.

 The Lewis model mainly shows electron distribution and bonding but does not accurately predict molecular shapes based on electron-pair repulsions—that role belongs to VSEPR theory.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following graphs illustrates the rate change in terms of change in reactant concentration with time?
options: Graph A (Concentration starts high, decreases rapidly then slows)
Graph B (Concentration starts low, increases rapidly then slows)
Graph C (Concentration starts high, increases slowly)
Graph D (Concentration starts low, decreases slowly)
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: The rate law for this reaction CO (g) + NO2 (g) --> CO2 (g) + NO (g) is rate = k[NO2]². Which one of the following could be a plausible mechanism for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following COULD NOT be considered as factor influencing the rate of chemical reaction?
options: The rate constant of the reaction
questions.explanation: The rate constant (k) is a parameter that quantifies the rate of a reaction at a given temperature; it is not an external factor that can be changed directly. Temperature, catalysts, and surface area of reactants are factors that influence the rate by affecting collisions and activation energy.

questions.questionText: In which of the following order of a reaction, a plot of ln[A]t versus time is a straight line whose slope is -k?
questions.explanation:
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is ln[A]t = ln[A]₀ - kt. Plotting ln[A]t versus time gives a straight line with a slope of -k.

 Zero-order reactions give [A]t versus time as straight lines, and second- and third-order reactions follow different integrated rate laws.

questions.questionText: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change of variable, the system shifts the equilibrium position in a way that tends to counteract this change of variable. This is a statement for
questions.explanation:
Le Chatelier's Principle states that if a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, temperature, or pressure, the system will adjust itself to partially counteract the effect of the disturbance and restore equilibrium. 

The other options refer to quantum mechanics and electron configuration rules.

questions.questionText: Which of the following CORRECTLY relates the vapor pressure of a liquid with its boiling point? Boiling point is
options: the temperature at which molecules present in the vapor phase go back to the liquid state.
the temperature at which the kinetic energy of molecules is much less than the intermolecular force.
the temperature at which all the three physical state co-exist.
the temperature at which the vapor pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.
questions.explanation:
The boiling point of a liquid is defined as the temperature at which its vapor pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure, allowing bubbles of vapor to form within the liquid.

 The first option describes condensation, the second is incorrect regarding energy comparison, and the third describes the triple point, not boiling.

questions.questionText: In a kinetic experiment, a student placed crystals of iodine in a closed reaction vessel, introduced a given quantity of hydrogen gas, and collected data to calculate the rate of formation of hydrogen iodide. What would be the effect observed on the rate of the reaction if the student takes twice the amount of iodine from that used in the first experiment?
options: The formation of hydrogen iodide will be decreased.
The rate of the reaction will be constant.
It speeds up the rate of the reaction.
It lowers the rate of the reaction.
questions.explanation:
The rate of a chemical reaction generally increases with the concentration of reactants. 

In the reaction H₂ + I₂ → 2HI, increasing the amount of iodine increases its concentration, leading to a higher collision frequency between H₂ and I₂ molecules, thereby speeding up the rate of formation of hydrogen iodide.

questions.questionText: Consider this equilibrium system: CO (g) + Fe3O4 (s) --> CO2 (g) + 3FeO (s). Which of the following disturbances shift the equilibrium position to the right?
questions.explanation:
According to Le Chatelier's Principle, if a change is imposed on a system at equilibrium, the position of the equilibrium will shift to counteract the change.

 We want a shift to the right (products).

questions.questionText: The speed with which a solute goes into solution is
questions.explanation:
The rate of dissolution refers to how fast a solute dissolves in a solvent. 

Extent of dissolution refers to how much solute can dissolve, degree of solvation refers to how well solvent molecules surround solute particles, and heat of solution is the energy change during dissolution.

questions.questionText: Which type of substances has the following general formula? (R1, R2 and R3 are hydrocarbon groups.)
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: What causes the momentary, temporary dipoles that give rise to London dispersion forces?
options: The large electronegativity difference between atoms.
The random, instantaneous movement of electrons.
The sharing of electrons between polar molecules.
The attraction of a positive ion to a negative ion.
questions.explanation: London forces originate from the brief, temporary fluctuations in electron distribution around a nucleus, creating instantaneous dipoles.

questions.questionText: In a triple bond (e.g., N2), the bond is composed of:
options: One sigma bond and two pi bonds.
Two sigma bonds and one pi bond.
questions.explanation: A triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.

questions.questionText: Which molecular geometry results when a central atom has four electron domains: two bonding pairs and two lone pairs?
questions.explanation: Four total electron domains gives a tetrahedral electron geometry, but two lone pairs result in a bent molecular geometry.

questions.questionText: The difference between the atomic radius and the ionic radius is most pronounced for:
questions.explanation:
Non-metals that form stable anions (e.g., F to F-) have a large increase in size (anionic radius > atomic radius) due to inter-electron repulsion.

 This makes the size difference very significant compared to the slight change in metals (cationic radius < atomic radius).

questions.questionText: Compared to non-polar molecules of similar mass, molecules that exhibit dipole-dipole forces typically have:
questions.explanation: Dipole-dipole forces are stronger than London forces (for comparable mass), requiring more energy to overcome, leading to higher boiling and melting points.

questions.questionText: The characteristic property of the elements in the f-block is:
options: Variable valency and color of ions.
Very similar chemical properties across the series.
questions.explanation: The f-block elements (Lanthanides and Actinides) have their f-orbitals filling in inner shells, resulting in very similar chemical properties because the outermost electrons (valence electrons) are virtually identical across the series.

questions.questionText: What is the unit of the rate constant (k) for a third-order reaction?
questions.explanation: For a third-order reaction (Order = 3), the general unit for k is (L mol⁻¹)² s⁻¹, which is (L mol¹)² s⁻¹, or L²mol²s¹.

questions.questionText: Which type of crystalline solid is typically an electrical insulator as a solid, but a good electrical conductor when dissolved in water or molten?
questions.explanation: Ionic solids are insulators in the solid state (fixed ions) but conduct electricity when molten or dissolved (mobile ions).

questions.questionText: What is the rate-determining step in a multi-step reaction?
options: The step with the lowest concentration of reactants.
The step with the highest value of the rate constant (k).
The step that occurs most frequently.
The elementary step with the largest activation energy.
questions.explanation: The rate-determining step is the slowest step, corresponding to the elementary step with the highest potential energy barrier (largest activation energy).

questions.questionText: A negative activation energy for a reaction would imply that:
options: The reaction rate decreases as temperature increases.
questions.explanation:
If Ea were negative, the Arrhenius equation would show that increasing T would make the exponent (minus Ea / RT) less negative (or more positive), resulting in a decrease in the rate constant (k).

 Thus, the rate would decrease as temperature increases, which is highly unusual and only occurs in very specific complex reactions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the largest radius: Atomic Radius, Cationic Radius, or Anionic Radius of the same element?
questions.explanation:
Anions are formed by gaining electrons, which increases electron-electron repulsion and expands the electron cloud, making the anionic radius larger than the neutral atomic radius.

 Cations are formed by losing electrons, which reduces repulsion and increases the effective nuclear charge, making the cationic radius the smallest.

questions.questionText: Which of the following explains why ionic solids are brittle?
options: The weak intermolecular forces between ions.
The free movement of delocalized electrons.
Displacement of a layer brings like-charged ions together, causing strong repulsion.
The large attractive forces between oppositely charged ions.
questions.explanation: When an ionic solid is struck, layers of ions shift, bringing positive ions next to other positive ions (and negative next to negative), leading to strong electrostatic repulsion and shattering (brittleness).

questions.questionText: What happens to the rate constant (k) of a reaction when the temperature is increased?
questions.explanation: According to the Arrhenius equation, as temperature (T) increases, the value of k increases exponentially.

questions.questionText: Which area of chemistry focuses on the study of the speed and pathway by which a chemical transformation occurs?
questions.explanation: Chemical Kinetics is the branch of chemistry that deals with the study of reaction rates and the detailed sequence of steps (mechanism) by which reactions occur.

questions.questionText: The relative ease of removal of an electron from a gaseous atom is measured by:
questions.explanation:
Ionization Energy is the minimum energy required to remove the outermost electron from a neutral, gaseous atom.

 A low IE means the electron is easily removed (high ease of removal).

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes the molecularity of an elementary reaction?
options: The overall order of the reaction.
The sum of the exponents in the overall rate law.
The number of reactant species that participate in the step.
questions.explanation:
Molecularity is defined as the number of reactant particles involved in a single elementary collision or step.

 It can be 1 (unimolecular), 2 (bimolecular), or 3 (termolecular).

questions.questionText:
Given the following heating curve:

In which region of the heating curve does heating of the liquid raises its temperature until the boiling point is reached?
questions.explanation: C to D represents heating the liquid, so its temperature rises until it reaches the boiling point.

questions.questionText: If the overall order of a reaction is 0.5, the reaction:
options: Is zero order in at least one reactant.
questions.explanation:
Elementary steps must have molecularity 1, 2, or 3, so their order must be an integer (1, 2, or 3). 

A fractional order (like 0.5) indicates the reaction must be a complex, multi-step process.

questions.questionText:
Given the equilibrium reaction:
2SO₃(g) ⇌ 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g)
At certain temperature, the equilibrium concentration of SO₃, SO₂ and O₂ are 0.4 M, 0.2 M and 0.1 M respectively. What is the value of the equilibrium constant for this reaction?
In which state of matter are most atoms stripped of their electrons, existing as a gaseous mixture of positive ions and electrons?
questions.explanation: Plasma is the fourth state of matter, an ionized gas that exists at extremely high temperatures where atoms are stripped of their electrons.

questions.questionText: If the temperature of a reaction is decreased, the rate of the reaction:
options: Increases due to higher collision frequency.
Decreases because fewer molecules can overcome the activation energy.
Remains constant, as only concentration affects rate.
Increases because the activation energy is lowered.
questions.explanation: Lowering the temperature reduces the average kinetic energy of the molecules, which significantly reduces the fraction of molecules with energy greater than Ea, resulting in a slower reaction rate.

questions.questionText: Which factor leads to the decrease in vapor pressure when a non-volatile solute is added to a solvent?
options: Increased kinetic energy of solvent molecules.
Reduced surface area of the solvent.
Solute particles blocking the escape of solvent molecules from the surface.
questions.explanation: The solute particles occupy space at the surface, reducing the fraction of solvent molecules that have enough energy to escape into the vapor phase, thus lowering the vapor pressure (Raoult's Law).

questions.questionText: The rate of a chemical reaction is defined as the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit:
questions.explanation: The reaction rate is defined as the change in concentration (usually measured in molarity) divided by the change in time (Rate = Delta [Concentration] / Delta Time).

questions.questionText: When a gas is cooled and compressed, it may liquefy. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the process of a gas changing into a liquid.

questions.questionText: For a reaction A + B → C, if the rate law is Rate = k[A]²[B], what is the overall order of the reaction?
questions.explanation: The overall order is the sum of the exponents in the rate law: 2 (for A) + 1 (for B) = 3.

questions.questionText: According to the Combined Gas Law, if the temperature is doubled and the volume is halved, the pressure of the gas will:
questions.explanation:
P2 equals P1 multiplied by (V1 divided by V2) multiplied by (T2 divided by T1).

 P2 equals P1 multiplied by (V1 divided by 0.5V1) multiplied by (2T1 divided by T1).

 P2 equals P1 multiplied by (2) multiplied by (2). P2 equals 4P1. The pressure will be quadrupled.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements CORRECTLY defines chemical bonding?
options: It is a force that holds atoms together in a compound.
It is the repulsive force between similar charges.
It is the process taking place during the evaporation of a compound.
It is a kind of chemical reaction taking place in matter.
questions.explanation: Chemical bonding is the attractive force that holds atoms or ions together in a compound.

questions.questionText: Which of the following obeys the octet rule for all of its constituent atoms?
questions.explanation: In CCl₄, carbon and all chlorine atoms have complete octets. The other species contain expanded octets.

questions.questionText: What fundamental principle is used to predict the direction of a shift in equilibrium when a stress is applied to the system?
options: The Law of Conservation of Energy
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier's Principle states that if a change of condition (stress) is applied to a system in equilibrium, the system shifts in a direction that relieves the stress.

questions.questionText: The ability of glass to break into irregular, non-geometric fragments when shattered is characteristic of its classification as a(n):
questions.explanation: Amorphous solids fracture randomly and unevenly because their atoms lack long-range order, while crystalline solids break cleanly along crystal planes.

questions.questionText: For a first-order reaction, how long does it take for the concentration to decrease by 50 percent?
questions.explanation: The time required for the concentration to decrease by 50 percent is the definition of the half-life.

questions.questionText: The forces holding atoms together in a covalent network solid like diamond are:
questions.explanation: Covalent network solids are defined by their vast network of strong covalent bonds.

questions.questionText: A gas occupies 10.0 liters at standard temperature and pressure (STP). If the temperature is doubled in Kelvin and the pressure is also doubled, what is the new volume of the gas?
questions.explanation:
Using the Combined Gas Law (P1V1 divided by T1 equals P2V2 divided by T2): If P and T are both doubled (P2 = 2P1 and T2 = 2T1), then (2P1)V2 divided by (2T1) equals P1V1 divided by T1.

 The factors of 2 cancel, meaning V2 equals V1. The new volume is 10.0 liters.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes a key characteristic of the half-life of a second-order reaction?
options: It is directly proportional to the rate constant.
It is independent of the initial concentration.
It decreases over the course of the reaction.
It is proportional to the square of the initial concentration.
questions.explanation:
For a second-order reaction, t half is proportional to 1 / [A]0.

 Since concentration [A] is continuously decreasing during the reaction, the half-life (t half) is continuously increasing (getting longer) as the reaction proceeds.

questions.questionText: The quantum number that describes the spatial orientation of an orbital is the:
questions.explanation:
The magnetic quantum number (ml) determines the orientation of the orbital in three-dimensional space.

 For instance, for l=1 (p-subshell), ml values of -1, 0, and 1 correspond to the px, py, and pz orbitals.

questions.questionText: The decomposition of phosphine on a hot tungsten surface at high pressure is a zero-order reaction. This means the rate is:
options: Proportional to the square of pressure
Independent of the concentration/pressure of phosphine
questions.explanation: In zero-order kinetics, the rate is constant and does not change regardless of the concentration of the reactant.

questions.questionText: A sample of solid chlorine (Cl2) has a very low melting point (minus 101 degrees Celsius). This suggests it is a:
questions.explanation: A very low melting point is characteristic of molecular crystals, which are held together by weak intermolecular forces.

questions.questionText: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a chemical reaction?
options: By increasing the temperature of the system
By providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
By shifting the equilibrium to the right
questions.explanation: Catalysts lower the activation energy barrier (Ea), allowing more molecules to have sufficient energy to react at a given temperature.

questions.questionText: Which type of intermolecular forces are the only forces that exist between noble gas atoms and non-polar molecules?
questions.explanation: Non-polar molecules and noble gases have no permanent dipoles, so their intermolecular attraction is due to London dispersion forces.

questions.questionText: The minimum energy required to start a chemical reaction by breaking existing bonds and initiating the formation of new ones is called the:
questions.explanation:
Activation Energy (Ea) is the energy barrier that must be overcome for reactants to transform into products.

 It is the minimum energy required for an effective collision.

questions.questionText: Which particle has a mass of approximately 1 atomic mass unit and a charge of 0?
questions.explanation: The neutron is a neutral (charge of 0) subatomic particle with a mass nearly equal to that of the proton, approximately 1 atomic mass unit (amu).

questions.questionText: The hybridization of the central atom in the molecular ion of tetrachloroiodate (ICl₄⁻) is sp³d². What is the geometrical shape of ICl₄⁻?
questions.explanation: ICl₄⁻ has 6 electron domains: 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs. The lone pairs occupy opposite positions, giving a square planar shape.

questions.questionText: What is the correct expression for the concentration equilibrium constant, K subscript c, for the reaction: 4NH₃ (g) + 5O₂ (g) is in equilibrium with 4NO (g) + 6H₂O (g)?
questions.explanation: K subscript c is the ratio of the product of product concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients to the product of reactant concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients: [Products] over [Reactants].

questions.questionText: The change in vapor pressure of a liquid with respect to temperature is best described as:
questions.explanation: Vapor pressure increases with temperature, but the relationship is exponential (non-linear), as described by the Clausius-Clapeyron equation.

questions.questionText: A phase change from gas directly to solid is known as:
questions.explanation: Deposition is the process where a gas changes directly to a solid, bypassing the liquid phase (the reverse of sublimation).

questions.questionText:
A student performed the following experiment during his laboratory session:
First: He added 25 mL of 2.0 M hydrochloric acid in each of two beakers
Second: He added 2.0 g of calcium to the first beaker
Third: He added 2.0 g of iron to the second beaker
Which of the following will be his observation?
options: It is not possible to observe any difference in reaction between the two beakers
The rates of chemical reaction in the first and second beakers are identical
fast chemical reaction is observed in the second beaker
fast chemical reaction is observed in the first beaker
questions.explanation: Calcium is much more reactive than iron, so it reacts faster and more vigorously with HCl.

questions.questionText: An anti-bonding molecular orbital (sigma star or pi star) is characterized by having a region of zero electron density, called a node, located:
options: At the nucleus of one atom.
Far away from the bonded atoms.
On the axis perpendicular to the internuclear axis.
questions.explanation: The node in an anti-bonding orbital is a plane of zero probability of finding an electron located between the nuclei.

questions.questionText: How does a catalyst speed up a chemical reaction without being consumed itself?
options: By providing a new pathway that increases temperature of reaction
By providing a new pathway that decreases temperature of reaction
By providing a new pathway that increases activation energy
By providing a new pathway that decreases activation energy
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy, increasing the reaction rate.

questions.questionText: The general property of elements whose atoms gain electrons easily is:
questions.explanation:
The tendency of an element to gain electrons is characteristic of its non-metallic nature.

 Non-metals typically have high electronegativity and high (exothermic) electron affinity, making them strong oxidizing agents.

questions.questionText: For a zero-order reaction, the rate constant (k) has the units:
questions.explanation:
For a zero-order reaction, Rate = k [A]° = k.

 Since the unit of rate is mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹, the unit of k must also be mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.questionText: What is the common property of the Noble Gases (Group 18)?
options: They exist as monoatomic gases at room temperature.
questions.explanation:
Noble gases have a stable octet (except He), making them chemically inert. 

They exist naturally as individual atoms that do not form molecules, hence they are monoatomic gases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following units represents the rate constant (k) for a first-order reaction?
questions.explanation:
For first-order, Rate = k[A].

 Thus, k = Rate / [A] = (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹) / (mol L⁻¹) = s⁻¹.

questions.questionText: In the Ideal Gas Law equation, what is the significance of the universal gas constant (R)?
options: It only relates pressure and temperature.
It relates the units of pressure, volume, temperature, and amount of gas.
It is a constant only for one mole of gas.
It is the same as the Boltzmann constant.
questions.explanation: The gas constant R is a proportionality constant that ensures the units in the Ideal Gas Law (PV equals nRT) are consistent.

questions.questionText: A solid substance is an electrical insulator as a solid, melts at a temperature below 100 degrees Celsius, and is soluble in a non-polar solvent. What is the most probable type of crystal?
questions.explanation: Low melting point and solubility in a non-polar solvent indicate a non-polar molecular solid.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes the nature of beta particles?
questions.explanation: Beta particles are high-energy, high-speed electrons or positrons that are emitted by certain types of radioactive nuclei, such as in beta decay.

questions.questionText: The scientist who used the oil drop experiment to determine the fundamental charge of the electron (e) was:
questions.explanation: Robert Millikan's oil drop experiment (1909) successfully measured the exact charge of a single electron, which, when combined with J.J. Thomson's charge-to-mass ratio, allowed for the calculation of the electron's mass.

questions.questionText: The volume of one mole of any ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP) is approximately:
questions.explanation: The molar volume of an ideal gas at STP (273.15 K and 1 atm) is 22.4 liters.

questions.questionText: Which crystal type is characterized by having positive and negative ions at the lattice points, which are held together by electrostatic forces?
questions.explanation: Ionic solids are composed of ions held together by ionic bonds (electrostatic attraction).

questions.questionText: The attractive forces between gas particles are only significant at low temperature and high pressure. This indicates that the KMT assumption regarding **intermolecular forces** is most inaccurate under these conditions.
questions.explanation: Low temperature slows particles down, allowing forces to act, and high pressure pushes them closer, increasing the force's effect, causing deviation from the ideal gas assumption of negligible forces.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between an intermediate and a transition state in a reaction mechanism?
options: The intermediate is a reactant, and the transition state is a product.
The intermediate is a stable molecule, while the transition state is an unstable, short-lived complex.
The intermediate is at the peak energy, and the transition state is at a valley.
The transition state is a catalyst, and the intermediate is a product.
questions.explanation:
A reaction intermediate exists in a potential energy valley (local minimum) and can sometimes be isolated.

 The transition state (activated complex) exists at the peak energy (local maximum) and is highly unstable and transient.

questions.questionText: Which type of reaction generally has the highest activation energy?
options: Reactions involving the breaking of multiple strong covalent bonds.
questions.explanation: Reactions that require the input of a large amount of energy to break strong chemical bonds (like multiple covalent bonds) will have a high activation energy.

questions.questionText: Which term describes the phase change from solid directly to gas?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the process where a solid turns directly into a gas without passing through the liquid phase.

questions.questionText: An ideal gas process occurs at constant temperature. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Isothermal means constant temperature (T).

questions.questionText: Which of Dalton's original postulates is retained as valid in the modern atomic theory?
options: Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties.
Atoms of one element are different from the atoms of all other elements.
Chemical reactions involve the combination, separation, or rearrangement of atoms.
questions.explanation:
Modern atomic theory acknowledges that atoms are divisible (subatomic particles), isotopes exist (differing mass), and nuclear reactions can change elements.

 However, the postulate that chemical reactions are simply the rearrangement of atoms remains valid for non-nuclear processes.

questions.questionText: Which type of bond is formed when one atom donates both electrons of the bond in a covalent bonding?
questions.explanation: A dative or coordinate covalent bond forms when one atom supplies both shared electrons.

questions.questionText: The type of crystalline solid where the fundamental units are atoms connected by covalent bonds that extend throughout the entire crystal is a:
questions.explanation: This description defines a Covalent Network solid.

questions.questionText: If the freezing point of water is 0 degrees Celsius, its melting point must be:
options: value that depends on the pressure.
questions.explanation: The melting point and the freezing point of a pure crystalline substance are the same temperature.

questions.questionText: The vapor pressure of all liquids at their normal boiling point is always equal to:
questions.explanation: The normal boiling point is the temperature at which vapor pressure equals 1 atmosphere, which is 760 mmHg.

questions.questionText: For a reaction to proceed through a bimolecular collision, what must be true about the activation energy?
options: The colliding molecules must have kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy.
The activation energy must be less than the enthalpy change.
questions.explanation:
Effective collisions require two factors: correct orientation and sufficient energy.

 The energy condition is that the kinetic energy of the colliding particles must be equal to or exceed the activation energy (Ea).

questions.questionText: Which type of solid exhibits a very high melting point and is a non-conductor of electricity due to localized electrons?
questions.explanation: Covalent network solids have strong covalent bonds throughout the entire structure, resulting in high melting points and poor conductivity (electrons are localized in the bonds).

questions.questionText: The most common oxidation state for a d-block element is typically:
questions.explanation:
Transition metals (d-block) generally exhibit the +2 oxidation state due to the loss of the two electrons from the outermost s-orbital (e.g., 4s electrons are lost before 3d electrons).

 Higher oxidation states are also common, but +2 is the most frequent starting point after Group 3.

questions.questionText: In the reaction profile, the species at the highest energy peak between reactants and products is the:
questions.explanation: The transition state (or activated complex) is the unstable, highest energy configuration that the reacting species must pass through to convert into products.
